statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Tail steps to 21% as NQ presses the session high, while Stress eases to 77% because the dollar and crude amplifiers have both decayed.
recommendation: Tail stays inside the watch band because NQ is pressing the session high on a band that widened only 2.5 points over the past hour, with no repeated extension after a failed retracement observed. Two amplifiers that supported the higher Stress reading have decayed: the dollar index is down 0.23% to 101.87 and WTI is down 1.65% to 91.34 at its session low, while the 10-year at 5.250% remains well below Thursday's 5.3445% peak. Stress stays high on long-end yields near 24-year peaks, a Hang Seng at an 11-week low and the September payrolls release at 12:30Z. The flagged window stays narrow, spanning 12:30Z to 15:00Z around the release and the U.S. cash open.
headline: NQ presses the overnight high on a barely wider band while the dollar and crude ease into the September payrolls print
body: NQ futures trade 30,920.50 (+0.52%, +160.00) as of 07:17Z inside an overnight range of 30,760.25-30,937.25. The session high extended only 2.5 points over the past hour, from 30,934.75, while price advanced about 46 points and now sits roughly 17 points below that high. The band is about 0.58% wide, so the structure is a contained upward drift rather than persistent directional efficiency, and no repeated extension after a failed retracement is observed. Price holding near the extreme is one amplifier, but the supporting cross-asset set has weakened rather than aligned. The 10-year Treasury yield is 5.250% against a 5.238% prior close in a 5.231-5.262 band, well below Thursday's 5.3445% print, which was the highest since 2002 after the bond market's worst quarter in decades; the 2-year is 4.796% against 4.787%. The dollar index has slipped 0.23% to 101.87 from 102.10 after reaching its highest since April 2025, and crude has fallen materially: WTI is 91.34 (-1.65%) and Brent 101.17 (-1.11%), both at session lows, as a rebound in Persian Gulf export flows offsets a continuing U.S. military build-up in the region. VIX closed at 16.39 and cash NDX closed 30,501.56 (+0.31%) on October 1 in a 30,274.65-30,616.24 range against a 52-week high of 30,770.63, with semiconductors leading after Micron's results. The clearest conflict is regional: the Hang Seng fell 3% to an 11-week low near 23,900 with Hang Seng TECH down 2.5%, the Nikkei lost 0.9% and the TOPIX 1%, while Australia and Korea gained and U.S. futures edged higher. Conflicting cross-asset evidence of this kind raises uncertainty rather than Tail. The dominant scheduled checkpoint is the September employment report at 12:30Z, with consensus near 89,000 jobs, unemployment seen steady at 4.1% and average hourly earnings at 0.3% month over month; October Fed hike odds are priced near 25%, down from about 69% a week ago, with a December move fully priced. Mode remains mixed: a narrow two-sided band with divergent regional equity and decaying rates, dollar and energy amplifiers. The shared Finviz context file was collected on September 29 at 23:14Z, which is far outside the 90-minute freshness limit and marked partial with futures and calendar sections unavailable, so it was treated as stale and contributed nothing to this assessment.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding published Claude hours stayed inside the watch band. Tail opened the window at 22% in the 07:00Z hour on October 1, peaked at 24% during the 14:00Z hour and has printed 20% for the last fifteen consecutive hours. Stress rose from 74% to a 79% overnight peak as the long-end yield selloff intensified, holding 78-79% through the Asian session, while Confidence stayed between 87% and 89% throughout.
outlookSummary: The forecast holds Tail at 21% through the European morning while the barely wider overnight band is assumed to keep containing price, steps it to 22-23% into the pre-release and release hours as depth thins, and reaches the 25% block threshold only conditionally for the 13:00Z and 14:00Z slots covering the U.S. cash open and the delayed-second-leg window after the payrolls print. That elevation is contingent on an aligned opening auction, shallow pullbacks and a long-end yield break back above 5.3445%, not on the release itself. Stress peaks in the extreme band at 83% around the cash open and decays through the afternoon as repricing completes. From 21:00Z the weekend CME halt means no live price path can form, so the remaining ten slots hold the 20% floor while Stress and Confidence step down to reflect a carried rather than observed assessment. The next live reference is the Sunday 22:00Z reopen and the next scheduled checkpoint is the ISM Services PMI on 5 October at 14:00Z, both outside this horizon.
